title: Magnetic and Thermal-sensitive Poly(N-isopropylacrylamide)-based Microgels for Magnetically Triggered Controlled Release
protocol: Add 14.02 g of FeCl3, 8.6 g of FeCl2·4H2O and 250 mL water to a 500-mL beaker.
Connect the rotor and controller to set up mechanic stirring.
Mix the solution at 300 rpm for 30 min at room temperature (RT).
Add 25 mL of ammonium hydroxide (33%) into the solution at RT and keep stirring (300 rpm) for 30 min.
Put a magnet under the beaker to collect the black particles.
Carefully remove the supernatant without shaking the beaker.
Add 50 mL of fresh water to the beaker.
Shake the beaker to re-disperse the Fe3O4.
Repeat washing steps three times to purify the Fe3O4.
Transfer all the Fe3O4 (10 g) into a 100-mL glass bottle.
Add water until the total solution volume is 100 mL.
Shake the glass bottle vigorously until no lumps are visible.
Transfer the 100-mL solution into a 1,000-mL beaker.
Add 10 mL of ammonia solution, 90 mL of water, and 900 mL of ethanol to the beaker.
Mix the solution at 300 rpm using a magnetic stir bar.
Add 500 µL of (3-aminopropyl)triethoxysilane dropwise to the beaker at room temperature.
Stir for another 12 hours.
Redisperse 1 g of Fe3O4-NH2 in a 20-mL glass bottle with 20 mL water.
Add 0.25 g of PNIPAAm, 5 mL of Fe3O4 solution, and 0.2 g of PEI to a 50-mL glass bottle for solution 1-1.
Add 20 mL of water to the 50-mL glass bottle for solution 1-1.
Stir at 300 rpm for 30 min using a magnetic stir bar for solution 1-1.
Repeat step for solution 1-1 but replace Fe3O4 with Fe3O4-NH2 solution for solution 1-2.
Add 0.8 g of PEI and 18.2 mL of water to a 50-mL glass bottle for solution 2.
Heat the solution up to 70 °C in a water bath for 30 min for solution 2.
Use an ultrasonic cell disruptor to sonicate (50 w) solution 2.
Stir solution 2 at 300 rpm using a magnetic stir bar and heat it to 70 °C.
Add Solution 1-1 dropwise to the heated solution 2 using a 3-mL syringe at a rate of 1 mL/min.
Continue sonication, stirring, and heating at 70 °C for 30 min.
Cool the solution to room temperature.
Remove the solution from the cell disruptor and water bath.
Place the magnet close to the glass bottle to collect the microgels.
Remove the supernatant after the microgels have precipitated to the bottom of the glass bottle.
Add another 25 mL of water to the glass bottle.
Re-disperse the microgels by vortexing.
Use an ultrasonic cell disruptor to sonicate Solution 1-2 at 50 w, a magnetic stir bar to stir at 300 rpm, and a water bath to heat Solution 2 at 70 °C.
Add Solution 1-2 dropwise to the heated Solution 2 using a 3-mL syringe at a rate of 1 mL/min.
Continue sonication, stirring, and heating for 30 min at 70 °C.
Cool the solution to room temperature.
Remove the solution from the cell disruptor and water bath.
Place the magnet close to the glass bottle to collect the microgels.
Once the microgels precipitate, remove the supernatant.
Add another 25 mL of water to the glass bottle.
Re-disperse the microgels by vortexing.
Stir 100 mg of Cur and 20 mL of ethanol solution in a dark environment at room temperature overnight.
Stir PNIPAAm/Fe3O4-NH2 at 400 rpm and room temperature overnight.
Use a magnet to collect PNIPAAm/Fe3O4-NH2 as described in steps 2.4.5 and 2.4.6.
Add another 25 mL of water to the glass bottle containing microgels.
Re-disperse the microgels by vortexing.
Place 10 mL of Cur-PNIPAAm/Fe3O4-NH2 solution in a 15-mL centrifugation tube.
Add 2 mL of water to the centrifugation tube.
Place the centrifugation tube in the center of the coil for applying HFMF20.
Apply HFMF at 15 KHz for 20 minutes.
Withdraw 0.5 mL of the HFMF solution and replace with fresh 0.5 mL of water every 2 minute interval during HFMF application.
Transfer the withdrawn solution to a 1-mL cuvette.
Measure the absorption of the withdrawn solution by UV/Vis at 482 nm.
Determine the concentration of released drugs using a standard calibration curve.
Heat PNIPAAm/Fe3O4 and PNIPAAm/Fe3O4-NH2 samples from room temperature to 100 °C under air atmosphere for weight loss measurement by TGA.
Keep the sample at 100 °C for 10 minutes to eliminate humidity.
Heat the sample from 100 °C to 800 °C at a rate of 10 °C/min.
Dry 10 mg of sample with 1 g of KBr at 100 °C overnight.
Grind the materials into a fine powder by using a mortar and pestle.
Place the assembled apparatus (mortar and pestle) into the pellet press.
Align the apparatus in the exact middle of the press.
Pump the press until a pressure of 20,000 psi is reached.
Let the pellet sit at that pressure for 5 min.
Remove the die containing the pellet and the piston from the press.
Turn it upside down and pump the piston to force the pellet out.
Record the FT-IR absorption spectra of samples by FT-IR at frequencies ranging from 400 to 4,000 cm-1 with 4 cm-1 resolution.
Drop the sample solution onto a copper-grid coated with collodion.
Dry the sample at room temperature or in a 70 °C oven overnight.
Take TEM images.
Add 7 mg of PNIPAAm and 7 mL of water to a 7-mL glass bottle.
Use a vortex to mix the PNIPAAm solution until there are no aggregates.
Transfer 0.7 mL of PNIPAAm/Fe3O4-NH2 solution to a 7-mL glass bottle.
Add 6.3 mL of water to the PNIPAAm/Fe3O4-NH2 solution in the 7-mL glass bottle.
Use a vortex to mix until there is no precipitation in the PNIPAAm/Fe3O4-NH2 solution.
Transfer 0.7 mL of Cur-PNIPAAm/Fe3O4-NH2 solution to a 7-mL glass bottle.
Add 6.3 mL of water to the Cur-PNIPAAm/Fe3O4-NH2 solution in the 7-mL glass bottle.
Use a vortex to mix until there is no precipitation in the Cur-PNIPAAm/Fe3O4-NH2 solution.
Place the PNIPAAm, PNIPAAm/Fe3O4-NH2, and Cur-PNIPAAm/Fe3O4-NH2 solutions into an oven at 70 °C.
Wait 2 h until equilibrium is reached in the solutions.
Take a picture of the solutions using a digital camera.
Place the strong magnet close to the Cur-PNIPAAm/Fe3O4-NH2 solution for magnetic collection of microgels.
Wait until the microgels are fully collected, then take a picture.
Remove the magnet and vortex the microgel solution until fully dispersed.
Take another picture.
